title: Find someone by a misspelled name or the last eight digits - once
summary: Support staff rarely have the exact spelling or the full number. Derived search gives them phonetic names and phone suffixes as NARROWING keys - and answers only when the answer is a single person. A key that matches two people returns nothing, which is what stops it becoming an enumeration tool.

steps.label: A customer with a name that has spelling variants
steps.note: Both features are OFF by default - each widens the search surface and adds token rows per contact, so switching them on is a deliberate act. This stack has them on.

steps.label: The exact identifier still works
steps.note: The baseline: an e-mail is an identifier, and identifiers resolve exactly.

assert.message: an exact lookup must return the same pseudonym the registration minted

steps.label: A name alone is refused
steps.note: Names are not identifiers: they are shared by many people, and answering on one would make the API a directory. A name may only NARROW a search that already has an identifier.

steps.label: The last eight digits, and only that
steps.note: The suffix is a keyed HMAC of the last eight digits - never the number. It answers because exactly one person in this scope matches. If two did, this would be a 404: a multi-hit is a miss, deliberately, so the endpoint cannot be walked to enumerate people.

assert.message: the suffix lookup must resolve to the same person

steps.label: A suffix that is too short is refused
steps.note: Fewer than eight digits would match too many people to be a narrowing key at all - so it is refused rather than answered vaguely.

steps.label: A suffix nobody has: a plain miss
steps.note: Absent and ambiguous look identical from outside. The caller learns 'not exactly one person here', never how many.

steps.label: The phonetic name narrows an identifier lookup
steps.note: The name is folded to a phonetic code, so common Croatian variants (Anic/Anić, Djuric/Đurić) land on the same key. It is still only a narrowing key beside the e-mail - never a search term on its own.
